newsitem.title: UK: Pifco says Kenwood rejects offer.
newsitem.headline: Pifco says Kenwood rejects offer.

text.p: Pifco Holdings Plc said on Thursday that Kenwood had rejected two of its recent proposals which called for a merger of the two companies.
Pifco added it was not at present in a position to make another offer for the company unless it had access to more detailed information on Kenwood's finances and management.
Both companies manufacture and distribute domestic electrical appliances.
Pifco said it had written to Kenwood in July with a proposal to merge the two businesses. The offer was informally updated in November before both were rejected, the company said.
Since then Kenwood reported on December 3, a decline of first-half pre-tax profits to 3.3 million stg from 5.56 million in the previous year.
Kenwood has been facing moves from rebel shareholders, led Brian Myerson and Julian Treger and their UK Active Value group aimed at selling the company.
In its statement on Thursday, Pifco said:"...Its (Kenwood) interim results...have highlighted some of the significant strategic and financial problems faced by Kenwood."
"In view of these problems... Pifco believes that at present it is not in a position to formulate an offer without access to more detailed financial information and to Kenwood's management.
The company, however, said it continued to believe that there was "sound commercial and industrial logic in a combination of Pifco and Kenwood".

If granted access to relevant information by Kenwood, it said it might be in a position to finalise the terms of an offer "which would be credible and could materially increase value for Kenwood shareholders".
